summary: Buildable: no errors, all 188 spec examples pass, all 5 open questions are non-blocking and no dev refinement question is a blocker. Before build, the product owner must decide 7 major dev refinement questions that change the tariff code, who is subject to source tax, or whether an employee can submit. The main one is the H-vs-A conflict on child row 22. Six technical leaks need wording fixes; some trace links are missing, and 8 items are inferred and need confirmation.

findings.title: Child row 22 contradicts the calculator: H or counted without H (A)?
findings.why: For a non-married employee's minor child who does not live in the household, the spec gives letter H. The calculator note says H applies only when the child lives in the household. This changes the tariff letter. The examples pass only because they test what the spec says.
findings.evidence: dev_refinement (major) on feature.md; AC-06.4.3; F-zh_source_tax_calculator-96658b; several AC-06.4.x/06.5.x examples marked '(to be verified)'; OQ-calculator-coverage
findings.action: Add a decision to decisions.yaml: row 22 gives 'counted without H' unless a domain expert confirms H with a calculator run. Fix AC-06.4.3 to match.

findings.title: Address reference date not defined
findings.why: For someone moving into or out of Switzerland, the address country decides whether they are subject to source tax, the canton, the cross-border questions and the tariff. The spec doesn't say whether the current address or the address from the first working day counts.
findings.action: Decide in decisions.yaml which address counts (recommended: the address from the first working day). Reword the home address question to match.

findings.title: Liechtenstein, more than 45 non-return days: double taxation note is missing
findings.why: The calculator returns the normal tariff code plus 'Unter Vorbehalt des Doppelbesteuerungsabkommens' (subject to the double taxation agreement). The spec records only the code, so HR loses this reservation.
findings.action: Decide that the tariff code is recorded together with the reservation note and an HR flag. Add an acceptance criterion to US-07.3/US-05.7.

findings.title: Required house number blocks some employees from submitting
findings.why: Addresses without a house number (rural addresses, building names, some foreign addresses) can't be submitted as written.
findings.action: Decide that the house number is optional, or allow an explicit 'no house number' choice. Update US-01.2.

findings.title: Liechtenstein residents are asked tariff questions whose answers are never used
findings.why: Residents who return daily, or have at most 45 non-return days, get no tariff code. They still answer the denomination, spouse and children questions, which goes against data minimisation (G-01).
findings.evidence: dev_refinement (major) on feature.md; G-01; US-08.4 step order (inferred, no cited fact)
findings.action: Decide whether the cross-border step comes first for Liechtenstein residents. Otherwise discard these answers on submission (extend D-036). Update the step order in US-08.4.

findings.title: Unclear who provides the first working day and what the employee sees
findings.why: HR says 'I ask them to confirm it', so a date set in advance by HR is likely. It is also undefined whether the employee sees derived results (insurance start date, fund civil status, tariff code). Both change the UI and the data flow.
findings.evidence: dev_refinement (major) on US-02.1 and US-05.7; trace_judge item.first_working_day (D-034)
findings.action: Add two decisions: (a) the date HR enters is shown at the start for the employee to confirm, or the employee enters it; (b) derived results are only for HR, or are shown to the employee before submitting.

findings.title: Technical leaks in the spec
findings.why: The text shows internal ids, rule-engine wording and interaction choices. Building them in limits engineering, and business readers can't follow the ids.
findings.evidence: tech_leak: feature.md ('child_*', 'rule permit_reminder', 'formal expression'); US-06.1 ('rule subject_to_source_tax', add/remove child blocks); US-08.2 (D-036 'may be kept' turned into a required re-display)
findings.action: Replace the ids with business names. State the need behind the child blocks ('capture answers for each child'). Reword AC-08.2.1 to match D-036 ('may be kept'), or record a decision that keeping them is required.

findings.title: Traceability gaps: claims or rows cite facts outside the cited set
findings.why: Unbacked statements weaken the cited knowledge model and can hide errors.
findings.evidence: trace_judge: 'H tariff' purpose on 8 child_* items; rows citing F-zh-52b67a, F-hr-b6d9b3, F-zh-e80d8f/ab4e1e (cross_border_tariff_applies, liechtenstein_no_source_tax_in_principle, source_tax_result); F-hr-d7431e (US-01.2, US-05.4); US-03.4 tariff letters; US-08.3 'date often moves'; US-08.4 nine-step order; item.address_country (D-010/D-038 not cited); fact_judge: F-zh-3058a4 garbled statement
findings.action: Add the missing fact or decision citations. Fix or remove the unbacked claims (for example, cite a fact for the H tariff purpose). Rewrite fact F-zh-3058a4.

findings.title: Non-blocking open questions and inferred items need sign-off before go-live
findings.why: The fund mapping, the canton for residents abroad and unverified calculator paths could produce wrong registrations or tariff codes.
findings.evidence: OQ-canton-abroad, OQ-civil-status-partnership, OQ-spouse-dob-other-status, OQ-calculator-coverage (D-009 go-live condition), OQ-nationality-wording; inferred: spouse_residence_country, spouse_nationality, child_tariff_result, US-04.2, US-06.3–06.5, US-08.4
findings.action: Assign a domain expert to check with Pensionskasse Muster and the Zurich calculator. Record the outcomes in decisions.yaml and mark the inferred items as confirmed.

findings.title: Smaller refinement gaps
findings.why: Without these there are no tests for rejected input, and some examples can't be tested as written.
findings.evidence: dev_refinement (minor): same item used as input and output (AC-08.4.2, AC-05.4.3); valid date ranges; 'has children = yes' with no child added, and a maximum number of children; mid-year estimate for the 60/45-day questions; country list, stateless people, several nationalities
findings.action: Fix the example tables. Add decisions on date ranges, at least one child when the answer is yes, the year basis for the day counts and the country list.
